texto: In the courtyard during the funeral wake, among mourners in black, Doña Leonor slaps Lupe across the face; the tray falls and the coffee cups shatter on the tiles; mourners gasp; Lupe holds her cheek, eyes full of tears.
The notary sits at the big desk and opens the leather folder; Doña Leonor sits stiffly in an armchair, Rodrigo stands behind her with his arms crossed, Valeria scrolls her phone, bored.
The notary lowers his glasses and looks up at Lupe, who is standing by the door holding a tray of coffee; slow push-in on Lupe; the cup slips from her hand and shatters on the floor.
Valeria bursts into an incredulous laugh and drops her phone on her lap; Rodrigo slams both hands on the desk, red with rage.
Doña Leonor rises and walks slowly to Lupe, grabs her chin with her red-nailed fingers and forces her to look up; Lupe trembles, tears running down.
Rodrigo leans over the desk threateningly toward the notary; the notary calmly closes the leather folder and holds his gaze.
Close-up of the notary speaking slowly; then Doña Leonor and Rodrigo exchange a long silent look full of hidden intentions.
Night: Lupe, crying, throws her few clothes into an old small suitcase on the iron bed; Emiliano stands in the doorway holding his hat against his chest.
Flashback with warm soft faded tones: frail Don Aurelio in bed holds Lupe's hand with both hands and looks at her with deep tenderness; Lupe, sitting at the bedside, is confused.
Doña Leonor stares into the fireplace holding a glass of tequila; Rodrigo paces behind her; she turns to him with an icy look.
Lupe opens her mother's small carved wooden box on the bed; under the rosary she finds the old sealed letter; she breaks the red wax with trembling fingers and reads, her hand over her mouth.
In the dark corridor, Doña Leonor stands pressed against the servant's door, listening; her face hardens, half lit by the light from under the door.
Lupe wipes away her tears, holds the letter against her chest, then takes her clothes back out of the suitcase; slow push-in as she looks at herself in a small mirror, determined for the first time.
